component.name: Apache Teaclave
component.description: Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) application ecosystem. The main branch of apache/teaclave is a landing page with no enclave, Trusted Application, or TEE code, so there is no trust boundary or Trusted Computing Base to audit on main itself; the security model document is a map to scanning targets. The active experimental-web3 branch hosts a TEE-backed crypto-wallet custody gateway (vm/wallet-gateway); the cleanroom (2022 prototype) and legacy (deprecated, with its own security docs) branches host SGX FaaS-style platforms. The authoritative trust-boundary methodology is the Teaclave SGX SDK, TrustZone SDK, and dependency-crates security models; the common rule is that the TEE side is trusted while the host OS, clients, network, external feeds, and persisted storage are attacker-controlled and must be validated at the boundary.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it. The document is intentionally brief: a map to scanning targets, not a full threat model; per-platform trust models live in the SDK repositories.

blueprints.name: Wallet gateway (experimental-web3 branch)
blueprints.description: The primary scanning target: a multi-crate wallet gateway custodying keys and signing blockchain transactions inside a TEE. The trust boundary is visible in the workspace layout: the task runner is split into a trusted half (task-runner-tee) and an untrusted host half (task-runner-normal), with the public edge, persistence, and outbound network on the untrusted side.

assets.name: task-runner-tee and key material
assets.description: The TCB: the trusted task runner and the key/credential material it handles (credential-manager, the signing/wallet logic). Private keys and plaintext must never leave it.

assets.name: api-server and webapi
assets.description: The public client-facing edge on the untrusted host; every client request entering it is attacker-controlled input.

assets.name: db-service / db-manager
assets.description: Persistence in untrusted storage; everything read back must be treated as adversarial and be encrypted/authenticated (sealed) before leaving the TEE.

assets.name: net (outbound calls)
assets.description: Outbound calls to external, attacker-influenced services such as blockchain RPC (net/.../btc_rpc.rs) and price oracles (net/.../asset_price.rs); external data is untrusted.

assets.name: task-runner-normal and authority-server host surface
assets.description: The untrusted half of the task runner; the boundary crossing between task-runner-normal and task-runner-tee is a focus for review.

zones.name: Trusted (inside the TEE)
zones.description: The TCB: task-runner-tee, credential-manager, and the signing/wallet logic.

zones.name: Untrusted (host / normal world)
zones.description: api-server, webapi, task-runner-normal, db-service/db-manager, net, and authority-server's host surface.

zones.name: External services and clients
zones.description: Clients of the public edge and external attacker-influenced services (blockchain RPC, price oracles).

assumptions.description: The main branch contains no TEE code (its crates/, sgx/, and trustzone/ directories hold only README showcase pointers); security scans should target the experimental-web3, cleanroom, and legacy branches.
Applications on these branches are built on the Teaclave TEE SDKs; the SDK security models (SGX SDK, TrustZone SDK, dependency crates) are the authoritative trust-boundary methodology when auditing.

The legacy branch carries its own security docs (docs/threat-model.md, docs/mutual-attestation.md, docs/service-internals.md, docs/access-control.md); do not duplicate them. cleanroom is an earlier prototype of the same untrusted app/ wrapper plus trusted enclave/ shape joined by mutually attested TLS.

threats.name: Wallet private keys or plaintext secrets leaving the TEE
threats.description: The key audit question for the wallet gateway: do wallet private keys and unencrypted secrets ever cross out of task-runner-tee? The TCB holds the signing and credential material; private keys and plaintext must never leave it.

threats.name: Signing or balance decisions based on unvalidated external feeds
threats.description: Every response from net (blockchain RPC, price feeds) is untrusted external data; a signing or balance decision must never be based on it without validation.

threats.name: Trusting data read back from untrusted storage
threats.description: Everything read back from db-service / db-manager lives in untrusted storage and must be encrypted/authenticated; reads are to be treated as adversarial. Key question: is data persisted by db-service sealed/authenticated before it leaves the TEE?

threats.name: Malicious client requests at the public edge
threats.description: Every client request entering api-server / webapi is attacker-controlled input a scanner should focus on, as is the boundary crossing between task-runner-normal and task-runner-tee.

trustBoundaries.name: TEE trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The common rule across all Teaclave trust models: the TEE side is trusted; everything else (host OS, clients, network, external feeds, persisted storage) is attacker-controlled and must be validated at the boundary.

trustBoundaries.name: External services boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Blockchain RPC and price oracle responses, and public client requests, enter the untrusted host from external, attacker-influenced parties.

controls.name: Validate everything crossing into the TEE
controls.description: Apply the SDK security models' common rule: treat the host OS, clients, the network, external feeds, and persisted storage as attacker-controlled and validate all data at the TEE boundary; keep private keys and plaintext inside task-runner-tee.

controls.name: Seal and authenticate persisted data
controls.description: Data persisted through db-service lives in untrusted storage; encrypt/authenticate (seal) it before it leaves the TEE and treat reads as adversarial.

controls.name: Validate external feed responses
controls.description: Validate blockchain RPC and price feed responses before they influence a signature or a balance; never base a signing or balance decision on unvalidated external data.
